about.title: Sanger Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and Fresno County's traffic data shows Sanger sees dozens of injury crashes each year, with at least one traffic death in the most recent reporting period. Corridors like Bethel Avenue and Annadale Avenue, along with Academy and Jensen Avenues, carry heavy local traffic, especially on Friday afternoons when reported collisions tend to peak. When a crash on one of these roads takes a loved one, California law gives certain family members the right to pursue a wrongful death claim against the responsible party. This is a civil matter, separate from any criminal charges the driver may face. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect grieving families in Sanger with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened, explain your options, and help you understand the timeline you're working with. There's no cost to you unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Sanger Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Can Be Confusing
items.desc: California law limits who can file a wrongful death claim, generally starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, before extending to other dependents or heirs. An attorney can help your family understand where you fit before any steps are taken.

items.title: A Strict Two-Year Clock
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window can be shorter if a government entity was involved, such as a public roadway defect. Waiting too long can close the door on a claim entirely.

items.title: Losses Beyond the Funeral Bill
items.desc: California allows families to seek recovery for funeral and burial costs, the financial support the loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. These losses are real, and an independent attorney can help make sure they're properly accounted for.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim after a crash in Sanger?
items.answer: Under California law, families generally have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If a government entity, such as a road maintained by Fresno County, is involved, the deadline can be much shorter. It's best to speak with an attorney as soon as you're able so no deadlines are missed.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: California law typically gives the surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children the first right to file. If none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be able to bring the claim. An independent attorney can review your family's situation and clarify who has standing.

items.question: What if the fatal crash happened on a busy Sanger road like Bethel Avenue or Annadale Avenue?
items.answer: Fatal and injury crashes are recorded across Sanger's higher-traffic corridors, and Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. see more reported collisions than other times. The specific road and circumstances of the crash can affect who may be liable, so an attorney will want to review the crash report and any available evidence. LawProactive can help connect you with someone who handles these details.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to help us find an attorney?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free service that connects injured families with an independent personal injury attorney. Attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your family recovers compensation. There's no cost or obligation just to talk and learn your options.
